title: Embed catalog zero-downtime swap strategy and per-tenant soft steering
creator: Aaliyah Chen
description: Design and implement a zero-downtime flow for introducing new embedding model variants into the catalog while preserving backward semantic compatibility and SLOs. This ticket covers a coordinated runtime + gateway strategy: catalog shadowing, per-tenant soft steering, KV-cache warmup, and a lightweight compatibility shim that can rerank or normalize distances when model embeddings shift. The goal is to make model swap operations non-disruptive for high-throughput embedding and reranking endpoints and to provide clear rollback criteria based on quality and latency deltas.
acceptance_criteria: New embedding variant can be placed into catalog in 'shadow' mode and receive 0% production traffic while collecting full telemetry
Can enable soft-steering per tenant to route a configurable fraction (0.1%–50%) of traffic to the new variant without changing client code
KV-cache warmup strategy reduces first-requests P95 token latency delta to <10% of baseline for warmed cohorts
A regression detector triggers automatic rollback if similarity-based recall on the canary cohort drops >1.5% absolute or latency SLO (P95) increases by >20%
Docs and Console UI surfaces the variant lifecycle (shadow -> soft-steer -> staged-rollout -> promote -> deprecate)
E2E integration test that simulates 10k concurrent embedding requests across 200 tenants passes with no more than 0.5% error budget burn relative to baseline
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Catalog shadowing - extend model metadata to support 'shadow' tag and telemetry-only routing (ENG gateway change + runtime opt-in)
Phase 2: Soft-steering control - add per-tenant routing weights and entropy-seeded traffic splitter in edge gateway (config + SDK flag)
Phase 3: KV-cache warmup - implement proactive warmup hook that replays representative prefix set for canary tenants into runtime caches
Phase 4: Compatibility shim - lightweight distance-scaling and rerank adapter that uses a small mapping model to align new-variant vectors to incumbent distribution
Phase 5: Safety automation - regression detector, automated pause/rollback runbook, and console alerting
Phase 6: Docs, SDK examples, and migration checklist for PMs and Solutions Engineers
rollout_plan: 1) Shadow period (2–7 days): route 0% real traffic, collect semantic deltas, latency breakdowns, and per-tenant distributions
2) Micro-canary (0.1% traffic): enable soft-steering for a randomized tenant subset; collect full metrics and semantic evals on stored prompt corpus
3) Tenant-gradualization (per-tenant ramp): allow tenant owners to opt-in via Console for 1% -> 5% -> 20% stepping with automated KPI checks between steps
4) Staged-rollout (50% traffic): if all KPIs stable, increase to 50% across non-SLA tenants while keeping enterprise tenants pinned to incumbent for 48 hours
5) Promote (100%): promotion requires semantic regression < 0.5% absolute and latency within SLOs for 72h; otherwise automatic rollback
6) Graceful deprecation: once promoted, set a deprecation window and run a phased retire with traffic shaping and customer notices
telemetry_and_alerting: Per-variant metrics: embed vector norms distribution, cosine similarity drift vs baseline, quantization fallback rates
SLOs: embedding encode P95 and P99, rerank end-to-end P95, and KV-cache hit rate per tenant
Semantic checks: daily evaluation job that computes recall@10 and nDCG on seeded prompt sets (dashboard: https://dashboard.redwood.ai/embeddings/variant-delta)
Automated regression alert: pager if recall@10 drops >1.5% absolute for canary cohort or if P95 latency increases >20%
Cost telemetry: per-variant CPU/GPU token cost estimate and projected monthly spend delta
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: New variant exhibits subtle semantic shift causing silent quality regressions. Mitigation: run cross-embed similarity mapping and hold hard-traffic for high-value tenants until gated evaluations pass.
Risk: KV-cache cold starts create high tail latency. Mitigation: KV warmup + preferential routing for initial requests, plus temporary quota to slow client retry storms.
Risk: Soft-steering causes skewed cost for tenants. Mitigation: per-tenant cost alerts and opt-out toggles in Console.
Risk: Mapping shim increases inference CPU. Mitigation: run mapping as a lightweight vector transform on the GPU where possible, or fall back to a quantized path with monitoring of compute burn
notes: This design favors safety and tenant autonomy over fastest possible promotion. We intentionally require per-tenant opt-in during early ramps for customers on Dedicated and Private deployments.
Compatibility shim is intentionally minimal — it should be an L2 adapter that can be turned off. If mapping models become large, prefer offline precompute for embeddings that back critical indexes.
We will coordinate with Solutions Engineering to build a 'preflight' evaluation service for large customers to test new variants against their private corpora before any traffic assignment
